analysis: Examined ClusterControlLeadership.swift, both base_text units; the head-side patch is only an excerpt. Changes: ClusterControlRequest gains an optional `stopsBefore: Int?` (head ~828-832, 836). ClusterControlReply gains `stopsAsked: Int?`. A new `ClusterOnboardingLeaderStatus.init(reply:)` extension maps the reply fields. All are plain Codable optional fields; older builds ignore them. The fields are pure data in this file. Leadership claim logic (supersedes order, lease/hand-over/take-over, leadershipConfirmed, solo grace) is unchanged, and no new decoding, parsing or privileged code path is added here. Since stopsBefore is only a serve-suppression hint carried on the pairing-keyed link control channel (S07), a forged value could at worst prevent a serve start. That would require an authenticated paired peer, so it is not a new trust boundary. A real concern would be a stale or attacker-supplied counter making the leader skip or force a serve. The enforcing logic, `OnboardingLive.localServe(unlessStoppedSince:)`, is outside the supplied evidence, so I could not verify it. Remaining questions for integration: (1) whether localServe fails safe when stopsBefore is nil, which leaves behavior as before; (2) whether the stopsAsked counter is persisted owner-only in ClusterSetupRecord; (3) whether the control channel authenticates the sender as a paired member before honoring the op. No concrete regression is visible in the supplied lines. The relevant threat models, A-018 availability and TB-012, concern the local add-on hold socket and do not apply to this cluster control channel directly.
